item.title: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.35
How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles Editor's Note American Airlines AAdvantage miles are some of my favorite rewards to earn and redeem. And there are plenty of ways to earn AAdvantage miles, whether you frequently fly American Airlines or earn miles through American Airlines credit cards and other partners. In fact, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) is currently offering its highest-ever welcome offer following its August refresh. For a limited time, the card has a welcome offer of 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. Whether you're sitting on a large balance already or considering this welcome offer, here's what you should know about redeeming American AAdvantage miles. How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for flights As with most airline miles, the best way to redeem AAdvantage miles is usually for flights. You can easily search and book one-way, round-trip and multicity itineraries operated by American Airlines and most of its partners on the American Airlines website or app. To do so, enter your origin, destination, travel date and number of passengers, plus whether you want to book one-way or round-trip. (If you want to book multicity, click "Advanced / multi-city search.") Then, click the "Redeem miles" box. Results for your search will appear. You can sort these results by award price, duration, arrival time and departure time. You can also filter the results by the number of stops, operating carrier and airport (for destinations with multiple nearby airports). And if you have flexible travel dates, you can click on "Calendar" to see how award rates on your route compare across the entire month. Once you find an award you like, click on its tile. A trip summary showing the itinerary and its cost in miles, and taxes and fees will load. You'll need to log into your AAdvantage account at this point if you haven't already. On the next page, enter or confirm the traveler's details and trip contact information. Click through to the next page to buy a mileage multiplier if you wish. Otherwise, you can select seats on the next page. On the following page, you can buy checked bags. Then, you'll reach the final booking page. You'll need to select whether to buy insurance before you can enter your payment information and ticket your trip. If you are flexible regarding your travel destination, you can use the award map feature. However, based on my experience, it often doesn't show all the lowest-priced award destinations you could book. I recommend using Seats.aero if you want to see broad ways to use AAdvantage miles from a particular origin. You can generally cancel an unused American Airlines AAdvantage award before departure and have your miles reinstated without a fee. You can also change many awards, though your itinerary may be repriced and require additional miles. Related: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for maximum value Redeeming AAdvantage miles for American Airlines flights AAdvantage prices American Airlines award flights dynamically, so there isn't a fixed award chart that defines how many miles these flights cost. Instead, the award cost of these flights can vary drastically based on date, departure time, when you book and more. For example, AAdvantage award flights can vary significantly in mileage cost, even on flights that are just a few hours apart. You can book Main Cabin economy award flights on American Airlines-operated flights, as well as premium economy, business-class and first-class awards, through AAdvantage. Of course, the cabins you can book on any given flight may vary based on what's available on that aircraft type and what American makes available for award bookings. Related: Can you transfer American Airlines AAdvantage miles? Redeeming AAdvantage miles for partner flights AAdvantage has Oneworld partners as well as non-Oneworld partners like Aer Lingus and Etihad Airways that you can book with American Airlines miles. While American-operated AAdvantage awards use dynamic award pricing, most partner awards follow the American Airlines AAdvantage partner award charts. And if even just one leg of your itinerary is operated by a partner, the award pricing will usually follow the partner award charts. For example, here's the AAdvantage partner award chart for one-way itineraries that start in the continental U.S. or Canada: | Destination | Main cabin off-peak | Main cabin | Premium economy | Business/first | First | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Contiguous 48 U.S. states and Canada | N/A | 12,500 miles | 22,500 miles | 25,000 miles | 50,000 miles | | Alaska | N/A | 15,000 miles | 25,000 miles | 30,000 miles | 55,000 miles | | Hawaii | N/A | 22,500 miles | 50,000 miles | 55,000 miles | 80,000 miles | | Caribbean, Mexico or Central America | N/A | 17,500 miles | N/A | 27,500 miles | 52,500 miles | | South America Region 1 | N/A | 20,000 miles | N/A | 30,000 miles | 55,000 miles | | South America Region 2 | N/A | 30,000 miles | 40,000 miles | 57,500 miles | 85,000 miles | | Europe | 22,500 miles | 30,000 miles | 40,000 miles | 57,500 miles | 85,000 miles | | Middle East | N/A | 40,000 miles | 62,500 miles | 70,000 miles | 115,000 miles | | Indian Subcontinent | N/A | 40,000 miles | 62,500 miles | 70,000 miles | 115,000 miles | | Africa | N/A | 40,000 miles | 65,000 miles | 75,000 miles | 120,000 miles | | Asia Region 1 | N/A | 35,000 miles | 50,000 miles | 60,000 miles | 80,000 miles | | Asia Region 2 | N/A | 37,500 miles | 50,000 miles | 70,000 miles | 110,000 miles | | South Pacific | N/A | 40,000 miles | 65,000 miles | 80,000 miles | 110,000 miles | However, there are always exclusions at the bottom of each AAdvantage partner award chart. For this one, business- and first-class awards that include travel on an aircraft with lie-flat seats in the U.S. and Canada cost 7,500 miles more than is shown. Plus, you can only travel in certain directions or transit certain regions when traveling to some regions. And unfortunately, not every partner award follows these rates. Awards operated by Fiji Airways and Air Tahiti Nui use dynamic pricing, so you may see rates significantly higher than those shown on the partner award chart. For example, a nonstop economy Fiji Airways flight might cost 28,000 miles one day and 100,000 miles the next. Additionally, it's worth remembering that the taxes and fees can vary drastically not only by route but also by operating airline. In particular, awards with segments operated by British Airways often have high taxes and fees. Luckily, you'll see the taxes and fees when you search for awards on the American Airlines website or app. Related: Why American Airlines AAdvantage has become my most valuable rewards currency Other ways to redeem AAdvantage miles It's usually best to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for flights, but you do have some other options. Flight upgrades You can redeem miles to upgrade American Airlines and Qantas flights. Head to the American Airlines website or app and find your trip to upgrade American Airlines flights. Once you open your trip, you'll likely see an upgrade offer under your trip details. In this case, I could redeem 63,900 miles or pay $584 for an upgrade on a three-hour flight. Redeeming miles for this upgrade would yield only 0.91 cents per mile, which is significantly less than TPG's September 2026 valuation of AAdvantage miles. For Qantas flights, you can request an upgrade with AAdvantage miles if you booked an eligible trip. You'll find out 24 hours before departure whether your upgrade has cleared. Head to this page to enter your confirmation code and last name to see if your trip is eligible. Seats on American Airlines-operated flights You can also redeem AAdvantage miles for seats on American-operated flights. In this example, you could redeem 7,300 to 8,300 miles or pay $70 to $80 for Main Cabin Extra seats. However, doing so will only give you 0.96 cents per mile, which is significantly lower than TPG's valuation of AAdvantage miles. Admirals Club access You can also redeem American miles for Admirals Club access in the form of a one-day pass or membership. One-day passes cost 7,900 AAdvantage miles or $79, while annual memberships that provide individual access to nearly 50 Admirals Club lounges cost 75,000 miles or $750. Meanwhile, annual memberships that provide access for you and up to two guests to more than 100 Admirals Club lounges and partner lounges worldwide vary as follows based on your AAdvantage elite status tier: - Member: 140,000 miles or $1,400 - Gold: 135,000 miles or $1,350 - Platinum: 130,000 miles or $1,300 - Platinum Pro: 125,000 miles or $1,250 - Executive Platinum: 120,000 miles or $1,200 As you can see, you'll only get 1 cent per mile when redeeming AAdvantage miles for an Admirals Club membership or a one-day pass. For many AAdvantage members, getting the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard — which provides the primary cardholder full membership access privileges to Admirals Club lounges — will be a much better option than redeeming miles for lounge access. Related: 3 reasons why this is the best card for Admirals Club lounge access Five Star Service You can also redeem American miles for Five Star Service at 16 U.S. airports if you have a first- or business-class ticket. Five Star Service provides: - Access to Flagship First check-in (or priority check-in if Flagship First check-in is unavailable) - Admirals Club lounge access - Personalized service through the airport - Priority boarding and reaccommodation - Car service coordination Five Star Service costs 35,000 miles or $350 for the first person, plus 10,000 miles or $100 per additional adult and 5,000 miles or $50 per child 17 and under if there are five or fewer people in your party. Otherwise, you'll need to pay an additional $350 for an additional Five Star Service greeter for every five additional travelers in your party. Related: A complete guide to VIP concierge services to upgrade your airport experience Hotel, rental car, cruise and vacation bookings It's also possible to redeem American miles for hotel bookings through the AAdvantage Hotels platform, rental cars through the AAdvantage Cars platform, cruises through the AAdvantage Cruises platform and vacation packages through the AAdvantage Vacations platform. However, these platforms are usually better used for earning miles and Loyalty Points than for redemptions, as they typically offer only 1 cent per mile or less. Experiences, gift cards and merchandise Finally, you can also redeem American miles for Ticketmaster tickets on the AAdvantage Events platform, merchandise through the AAdvantage Exchange platform and gift cards through the AAdvantage Gift Cards platform. And if you are a Citi / AAdvantage cardholder, you can redeem American miles to book Mastercard Priceless experiences. However, don't expect any of these options to give you outsize value. Even with an AAdvantage cardholder discount, I'd still only get 0.7 cents per mile when redeeming for an Amazon gift card. Related: The 8 best ways to redeem up to 100,000 American Airlines AAdvantage miles How much are American Airlines AAdvantage miles worth? Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, American AAdvantage miles are worth 1.45 cents each. This valuation is based on the AAdvantage awards Points Path users saw during searches over a three-month window before the valuations were published. As such, it represents the value you can get from AAdvantage miles if you don't try to maximize them. As a reminder, you can compare your redemption rate — the comparable paid rate minus the taxes and fees you'd pay on the award, all divided by the award's mileage cost — to TPG's valuation to determine whether you're getting decent value on your redemption. American Airlines AAdvantage prices its own flights dynamically, but you may still see some very high or low redemption rates. Meanwhile, partner-operated awards that follow an award chart may offer poor value on some routes but outsize value on others. In particular, you can often get great value when booking long-haul premium cabin awards operated by partner airlines like Qatar Airways and Japan Airlines. Related: How TPG determines its points and miles valuations Bottom line American Airlines AAdvantage miles can be extremely useful, especially since you can redeem them for flights on American and a wide range of partner airlines. American-operated awards use dynamic pricing, while most partner awards still start at published award chart rates. So, having flexible travel dates and comparing your options can help you stretch your miles further. You can also redeem AAdvantage miles for upgrades, seats, Admirals Club access, hotels, rental cars, cruises, vacation packages and more. However, many of these options only give a redemption rate of 1 cent per mile or less. So, I prefer to save my AAdvantage miles for flights, including high-value partner-operated awards. Frequently asked questions American Airlines AAdvantage says its flights start at 7,500 miles each way, although you'll occasionally find less-expensive awards. American uses dynamic pricing for its flights, while most partner awards start at the rates shown on American's partner award charts. You can redeem AAdvantage miles for flights on American's Oneworld partners, as well as non-Oneworld partners such as Aer Lingus and Etihad Airways. Most of these partner awards follow American's partner award charts, although Fiji Airways and Air Tahiti Nui awards use dynamic pricing. You can usually cancel an unused AAdvantage award before departure and have your miles reinstated without a fee. Many awards can also be changed, though the new itinerary may be repriced and require additional miles. TPG values American Airlines AAdvantage miles at 1.45 cents each as of September 2026. Your actual redemption value can vary significantly depending on the award, with some partner premium cabin awards offering significantly more value. You can redeem AAdvantage miles for hotels through AAdvantage Hotels and rental cars through AAdvantage Cars. You can also use miles for cruises and vacation packages, but these redemptions typically offer around 1 cent per mile or less.

item.title: Deal alert: Points and miles travel deals for September 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.59
Deal alert: Points and miles travel deals for September 2026 Editor's Note From bonus points on your next hotel stay to sales on award tickets, we're always looking for travel deals that help you earn more points and miles and redeem them for maximum value. In other words, we want to help you book the vacation of your dreams. This time around, we've got some valuable new perks on an under-the-radar airline credit card and a offer that could save you $200 on a ski trip. Delta SkyMiles and World of Hyatt members can earn more rewards with this exciting new partnership. And don't forget to activate your Q3 bonus categories on this fan-favorite credit card. Each week, we help our readers by rounding up promotions so they don't have to scour the internet for the best reward redemptions and offers. This includes everything from frequent flyer programs and hotel rewards programs to credit card offers and rental car deals. Here's our latest list of noteworthy new points and miles promotions for September. Below is one of the best offers we found for September. Register and book by Sept. 15 for travel through Dec. 10. Plus, you'll be allowed one free date change on eligible bookings made during the offer period (fare difference may apply). Travel must be completed by Dec. 10, 2026, for one-way flights or May 31, 2027, for round-trip flights. You can score 20,000 bonus points — worth $150 by our valuations — on a vacation package of three-plus nights in Hawaii or Mexico through Vacations by Marriott Bonvoy. Book by Sept. 30, 2026, for travel through March 31, 2027. The Marriott deals don't end there. Bonvoy members can also earn up to 4,500 bonus points per qualifying stay: 1,500 bonus points when you stay two or more nights, plus an additional 3,000 bonus points at resort properties. Register by Nov. 13 for stays from Sept. 22 through Nov. 22. Be sure to check your Amex account before you book, as we've seen some targeted Amex Offers to help you save on Marriott purchases. Related: Best hotel credit cards Rental car promotions (September 2026) Summer may be almost over, but that doesn't mean you can't take an epic road trip. This rental car deal can help you save this fall. Get your fifth day free with Hertz Hertz is offering a fifth day free when you book an SUV or minivan for 4-27 days at participating Hertz locations in the U.S. This applies only to the base rate; taxes and fees are excluded. Book with promo code 212109 and pick up your vehicle by Dec. 31. Don't forget to stack this deal with any perks or elite status you may have at Hertz through your credit card. Credit card promotions (September 2026) Card issuers offer deals and discounts on a wide range of products, from airfare to dining. Here are some of the offers we've rounded up this week. Note that these are targeted, so they may or may not be available on your account. You must activate these offers on your card and use the enrolled card to make the purchase in order to earn bonus rewards. Targeted Amex Offer at Marriott If a Marriott stay is in your future, check your Amex account. Targeted cardholders can earn $200 back when they spend $450 or more at participating Marriott Bonvoy properties in the U.S., Canada, Mexico and the Caribbean by Nov. 30 — potentially saving you up to 44%. Targeted Amex Offer on cruises Ready to sail away on your next adventure? This Amex Offer, which we spotted on the American Express® Gold Card, could help you save at Holland America. Get a $200 statement credit after you spend a minimum of $750 in one or more qualifying Holland America purchases of cruise reservations. Book online, by phone at 1-877-932-4259, or through a Holland America travel advisor by Oct. 22. Targeted Amex Offer at Europcar If you're targeted, this Europcar offer could save you money on a rental car. Related: The ultimate guide to saving money with Amex Offers Ongoing travel deals In addition to these new offers, many others from previous weeks are still available: - If you live in Washington State, you can earn one Delta SkyMile for every passing yard the Seahawks complete this season. Sign up to start earning. - Until Sept. 30, earn 25 AAdvantage bonus miles for every dollar you give online on donations of $25 or more. You can double your bonus miles by paying with an American Airlines cobranded card. - Earn 3,000 bonus World of Hyatt points per stay — up to 30,000 total — when you spend at least three nights at participating Hyatt Place and Hyatt Select hotels in the U.S., Canada, the Caribbean and Latin America. Book with code "S2449" and stay by Sept. 30. - Save up to 25% on award flights to and from Europe with Flying Blue's September Promo Rewards. Book by Sept. 30, 2026, and travel by Feb. 28, 2027. - Through Sept. 30, you can double your Hyatt points on eligible dine-in and takeaway spending at participating Hyatt restaurants and bars across Asia Pacific with this promotion. - Earn 5,000 bonus points when you complete a stay at any Bonvoy hotel by Sept. 30. item.title: Atmos Summit card: Why it's the most rewarding airline card to maximize international travel
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.44
Atmos Summit card: Why it's the most rewarding airline card to maximize international travel If the Atmos Rewards loyalty program isn't on your radar yet, it's time to buckle up and pay attention. Born from the merger of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, this program has quietly become one of the most valuable in the industry, with an award chart full of sweet spots. And the premium Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card is the best way to quickly rack up those points, especially if you travel internationally. That's because, in addition to the impressive welcome bonus, the Summit card earns an impressive 3 Atmos Rewards points per dollar spent on foreign purchases. That's not just dining or travel, but every purchase made in a foreign currency. When you're traveling abroad, the last thing you want is to have to figure out which card to use for each transaction. With the Summit card, it's all you need. Here's why this single earning rate makes the card the market leader for international travelers. Atmos Rewards Summit Visa Infinite credit card: Earn 80,000 bonus points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $4,000 or more on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. Related: My take on Alaska's unified Atmos Rewards program Why the Summit's foreign purchases earning rate puts this card in a league of its own At TPG's September 2026 valuation of Atmos Rewards points, earning 3 points per dollar on foreign purchases translates to 4.65 cents of value per dollar spent abroad. Eligible Bank of America account holders can do even better, receiving a 10% rewards bonus on points earned from card purchases. That boosts the return on eligible foreign transactions to 3.3 Atmos Rewards points per dollar, worth about 5.12 cents per dollar at TPG's September 2026 valuation. That's an exceptional return on purchases that would otherwise fall outside other airline cards' bonus categories. The beauty of the Summit card is its simplicity. There are no rotating categories to activate, no cap on bonus earnings and no confusion about merchant codes or time zones. Every eligible foreign transaction earns the same generous rate, whether you're paying for a hotel in Tokyo, a train ticket in Switzerland or groceries in Mexico. TPG contributing editor Matt Moffitt, who recently relocated to Spain, now uses the Summit card for all non-dining purchases. Though the American Express® Gold Card still edges ahead in one single category, dining at 4 points per dollar spent at restaurants worldwide (on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, the 1 point per dollar spent thereafter), Amex acceptance outside the U.S. can be inconsistent, something Matt doesn't face with the Summit's worldwide Visa network. How the Atmos Summit compares with other premium airline cards' international earning rates The Summit card earns: - Unlimited 3 points per dollar spent on eligible worldwide dining, Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines purchases and all foreign transactions - Unlimited 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases (such as supermarkets within the United States) The card has an annual fee of $395. Most premium airline cards with similar annual fees offer bonus points or miles in a limited number of select travel categories and 1 point or mile per dollar spent on everything else, but none match the Summit's blanket 3 points per dollar spent on foreign purchases: - The Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® with a $350 annual fee (see rates and fees) earns 6 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings, 3 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases, but only 2 miles per dollar spent on dining and eligible "Rides and Rails", and just 1 mile per dollar spent on other purchases. - The Delta SkyMiles® Platinum American Express Card with a $350 annual fee (see rates and fees) earns a similar 3 miles per dollar spent on Delta purchases and purchases made directly with hotels, but only 2 miles per dollar spent on restaurants worldwide including takeout and delivery in the U.S., and at U.S. supermarkets, and 1 mile per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. - The United Quest℠ Card with a $350 annual fee (see rates and fees) earns 5 miles per dollar on prepaid hotel stays booked through Renowned Hotels and Resorts, 4 miles per dollar spent on eligible United flights, 4 miles per dollar spent on all other United purchases, 2 miles per dollar spent on dining, select streaming services and other travel, and 1 mile per dollar spent on all other purchases. None of these cards comprehensively reward the routine spending that makes up the bulk of what travelers actually charge abroad: groceries, transportation, shopping and incidental expenses. Meanwhile, the Summit card generously and innovatively rewards you for being an international traveler. Other Atmos Summit benefits The foreign-earnings rate is my favorite feature, but the Summit's broader offering justifies its $395 annual fee for frequent travelers, whether they travel domestically or internationally. The current welcome offer delivers decent value: earn 80,000 bonus Atmos Rewards points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $4,000 or more on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. The Global Companion Award offers a discount of up to 25,000 points (or 100,000 points after $60,000 or more on purchases each anniversary year) on the second passenger's ticket when you book two people traveling together with Atmos Rewards points. Uniquely, it is valid for travel on Alaska Airlines and all of its airline redemption partners, both in and outside of the Oneworld alliance, in any cabin — including Hawaiian Airlines, British Airways, Qantas, Iberia, Icelandair, Korean Air and others. Applicable fees and taxes still apply. The card also offers a host of other travel benefits, including anniversary status points, a pathway to elite status, lounge and Wi-Fi passes, waived same-day confirmed flight change fee and free checked baggage on Alaska and Hawaiian flights. You don't need to fly Alaska to get amazing value from Atmos Rewards points Even if you've never flown Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines, Atmos Rewards points can deliver amazing value through partner redemptions. The program inherited Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan's award chart, which has long been a favorite among points and miles enthusiasts for its outsize value on partner airlines. The sweet spots span virtually every region of the globe. You can book an American Airlines flight of up to 700 miles in length for just 4,500 Atmos Rewards points, or fly Hawaiian Airlines economy from the West Coast to Hawaii from 10,000 points. Looking to cross the Atlantic? Aer Lingus business class to Ireland starts at just 45,000 points. For aspirational redemptions, 75,000 points can get you a seat on Japan Airlines' business class from the West Coast to Tokyo, or Fiji Airways business class to Fiji. Bottom line Earning 3 Atmos Rewards points per dollar spent on every eligible transaction abroad — worth 4.65 cents per dollar at TPG's September 2026 valuations — is unmatched by any other airline card. If you haven't been paying attention to Atmos Rewards, consider this your wake-up call. With broad earning abroad, useful travel perks and a valuable partner redemption chart, the Atmos Rewards Summit card is an incredible companion to pack with your passport. And right now, the card is offering a great welcome offer: Earn 80,000 bonus points and a 25,000-point Global Companion Award after spending $4,000 or more on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. If international travel is part of your life, this card should be, too. Apply here: Atmos Rewards Summit Visa Infinite credit card Related reading: - How to reach Alaska Airlines elite status with just 1 card - Is the Atmos Rewards Summit worth the annual fee? - Why American Airlines flyers should pay attention to Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards - Who are Alaska Airlines' partners? Plus, how to earn and redeem Atmos Rewards points For rates and fees of the Delta Platinum Amex, click here.

item.title: Worth the upcharge? Flying Singapore Airlines premium economy
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.91
Worth the upcharge? Flying Singapore Airlines premium economy Quick take: Singapore Airlines is a comfortable way to fly long distances if you can't find business- or first-class awards that work for your budget. Pros - Comfortable seats have a lot of recline. - Passengers can preorder "Book the Cook" meals. - There's great entertainment and free Wi-Fi for KrisFlyer members. Cons - There are few seats per plane and high award prices. - Some seat features are not ergonomic. - Certain elements, like plastic cups, don't feel elevated. I first flew Singapore Airlines premium economy over a decade ago, shortly after the carrier introduced the new cabin. Although I've since flown Singapore Airlines premium economy on a handful of short routes within Asia, I was excited to try the service again on a longer jaunt. So, when I saw an award ticket on the eight-hour route from Melbourne to Singapore, I cashed in some Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer miles for a ticket. While my flight was between Australia and Asia, Singapore Airlines has installed the same premium economy seats on its long-haul Boeing 777s, Airbus A350s and A380s. In other words, the plane I flew is similar to what you'll find on the airline's longest routes, as is the service on board. Here's my experience flying Singapore Airlines premium economy, and how you can book it for yourself. How much does it cost to book Singapore Airlines premium economy? The cost of a long-haul flight in Singapore Airlines premium economy depends on the route, dates and whether you're flying round-trip or one-way. My one-way flight from Melbourne Airport (MEL) to Singapore Changi Airport (SIN) would have cost $2,784.25 Australian dollars ($1,995), which was pretty steep. An economy ticket would have cost AU$1,457.25 ($990), so my ticket was around twice as expensive. Just for context, a business-class ticket on my flight would have cost AU$4,246.25 ($3,042), just over $1,000 more than premium economy. In terms of mileage prices ... it gets more complicated since Singapore Airlines introduced semi-dynamic "Access" pricing. Let me try to snapshot it for you, though: | Cabin | Cash price | Saver award | Advantage award | Access award | |---|---|---|---|---| | Economy | $990 | 29,000 | 60,500 | 87,000 | | Premium economy | $1,995 | 53,500 | Not published | 94,500 | | Business | $3,042 | 72,000 | 103,500 | 160,000-213,500 | | First | $4,251 | 98,000 | 178,500 | 331,000 | As you can see, mileage prices vary not just widely, but wildly. You could get a first-class ticket that costs over twice as much as a premium economy ticket for just a few more miles if you found a Saver award (one was available the week I flew) versus an Access award in premium economy. In my particular circumstances, I could only find Access awards in all classes on the date I needed to travel. That meant an economy award would have cost 87,000 miles, but a premium economy ticket that would have been twice as expensive in dollars was just 7,500 more miles. So, I decided to book premium economy. I was hoping a business-class saver-level award would become available, but the lowest those fell to was 192,000 miles — most definitely out of my budget. All told, I spent 94,500 KrisFlyer miles plus AU$114.25 ($77.65). That pegged my per-mile value at 2 cents apiece, which is well above TPG's September valuation of Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer miles at 1.3 cents each. To think about it a different way, I got a ticket that would have been $1,005 more expensive for just 7,500 more miles. So the value of each additional mile I redeemed was more like a whopping 13.4 cents. Don't have a ton of Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer miles? It's easy to stock up on them since the program is a 1:1 transfer partner of the following credit card rewards programs: While it still pained me to spend over 94,000 miles on my ticket, it still felt like an OK deal given the eight-hour flight duration, the ready availability of award tickets and the ease with which I can earn KrisFlyer miles. Checking into and boarding Singapore Airlines premium economy Singapore Airlines premium economy passengers can enjoy the following priority services at the airport: | Dedicated check-in | Yes | |---|---| | Luggage allowance | Two checked bags up to 23 kg (50 pounds) each or up to 35 kg (77 pounds) total | | Lounge access | No | | Does the airline participate in TSA PreCheck? | Yes | | Priority boarding | Yes, Group 3 | I arrived at the Melbourne airport exactly two hours before my 9:15 a.m. flight and found only a few other passengers waiting in line to check in with agents. There were dedicated lines for economy, premium economy, business class and first class, so I stepped into the lane for premium economy and was helped immediately. My bag was tagged, my boarding pass was printed, and I was directed to security and immigration. Unfortunately, Singapore Airlines premium economy passengers do not receive lounge access, but there are a few Priority Pass options for folks with access to that network. I stopped by the Aspire lounge for a cappuccino, but then went to the gate for boarding, which started right on time at 8:30 a.m. How comfortable is Singapore Airlines premium economy? Singapore Airlines' premium economy is between the business-class and economy cabins on the 777. Passengers can board through the main door, which is just forward of the main business-class cabin — the same door the economy folks board through. | Number of seats | 28 | |---|---| | Cabin layout | 2-4-2 | | Seat pitch | 38 inches | | Seat recline | Up to 8 inches | | Seat width | 19.5 inches | | Screen size | 13.3 inches | The premium economy cabin comprises 28 seats total in a 2-4-2 pattern. There are three rows of two seats each along either side of the cabin and four rows of four seats running down the center. For families of up to four, those center sections are ideal, while couples should enjoy the two-seat sections. The seats have 38 inches of pitch and are 19 1/2 inches wide between armrests, which feels much roomier than the 18-inch-wide economy seats (which are in a 3-3-3 pattern). That said, my bulkhead seat was effectively an exit row place and felt a little narrower due to the curvature of the cabin wall. There are just two manual (non-electronic) buttons to control the seat: one to recline the seatback up to 8 inches, which feels very expansive, and one to raise the legrest. My bulkhead seat's legrest had an attached pop-out footrest, though those in the other rows have footrests attached to the seat in front, which might affect the size of the bag you can put there. The tray tables are stowed in the center consoles between seats. There is a cover you have to open to access them, and the finger hold you use to do so is blocked by the table when it's deployed, so it can be a bit of a rigmarole. However, the tray table itself is very substantial and easily fit my MacBook Air plus a beverage with no issue. Beneath the control buttons, there is a corded touchscreen remote for the entertainment system, plus a small stowage cubby for little items like classes or a phone. There is a larger shelf next to the legrest where my computer could fit while I charged it. Speaking of plugs, there was an easily accessible USB-A port in the island where the entertainment monitors were stowed. There was also a universal power port embedded next to the seat's legrest. A second USB-A plug behind the armrest was handy for keeping wires out of the way. Just above that was an adjustable attached reading light. There were no USB-C ports, unfortunately. Premium economy passengers share five lavatories with the 184 folks in economy. Two were behind the first economy cabin, to either side of a small galley. The other three were at the back of the plane near the larger galley. Though they did not get too busy during most of the flight, there were huge lines for all of them after meal times. That said, the crew kept them very clean throughout the flight. Amenities in Singapore Airlines premium economy Each seat in Singapore Airlines premium economy came stocked with a medium-size pillow in eye-catching orange and a light fleece blanket. Since there weren't individual overhead air nozzles and the cabin was temperate, I didn't need my blanket. Amenity kits are available on request and include: - An eye mask - Slippers - Lip balm - A pouch made from recycled paper fabric The seat's entertainment screen measured 13.3 inches across diagonally. It offered hundreds of movies and TV shows, including recent releases like "The Devil Wears Prada 2," "The Mandalorian and Grogu," and "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie." Among the TV shows were "Dutton Ranch" and "House of the Dragon." The screens on most seats were mounted in the preceding seatback and tilted up or down slightly for better viewing when reclined or upright. The screen for my bulkhead seat was stowed in an island between the seats and popped up on a metal arm, then swiveled right and left from there. So, I couldn't use it for takeoff and landing. Some wear and tear meant it sort of sagged downward on the unattached side, but it didn't really impede my viewing. The center bulkhead seats have their monitors mounted on the cabin wall in front of them. The airline provided basic noise-canceling headphones that plugged into a jack near the USB port at the back of the armrest. It wasn't easy to plug the headset in, but once it was, the positioning meant the cord was mostly out of the way. Singapore Airlines offers Wi-Fi on its 777s. You can purchase a paid plan at the following rates: - One hour: $3.99 - Three hours: $8.99 - Full flight: $15.99 Business-class and first-class passengers, as well as elite PPS members, receive free Wi-Fi. Even better, if your KrisFlyer account is linked to your reservation, you can access free, unlimited Wi-Fi on multiple devices at once by entering your last name and seat number. I found the Wi-Fi good enough to do a little web surfing, but uploading a short video clip to Instagram took over an hour. Fast.com clocked the speed at 280 Kbps. How was the food in Singapore Airlines premium economy? Although there were no predeparture beverages, the attendants came through with the first beverage service and passed out packets of mixed almonds and cashews about 20 minutes into the flight. Passengers could choose from a selection of soft drinks, water, juice, beer and small bottles of spirits. The small, but respectable, wine list included: - Charles de Cazanove Brut Champagne - Craggy Range sauvignon blanc from Martinborough, New Zealand - St. Hallett Faith Shiraz from Australia's Barossa region On my eight-hour daytime flight, the meal service in premium economy included lunch and a light pre-landing snack — pretty much the same as you'd find in economy. However, premium passengers could take advantage of the airline's famous "Book the Cook" service (bookable up to 24 hours in advance), though the options were more limited than those in business and first class. I "booked the cook" in advance, selecting poached chicken with ginger and spring onion relish over steamed jasmine rice and served with Chinese cabbage and carrots. The whole meal was served on one tray and accompanied by a starter of melon and prosciutto over arugula, a garlic roll with butter, Arnott crackers with cheddar cheese and an apple cake with lemon curd. It basically felt like an economy meal, but the plateware had a ceramic-like finish, which elevated the look, and the metal cutlery did the same, though the cups used in premium economy were all plastic. The dish was flavorful but not super substantial. Still, it made for a tasty light lunch. Among the options available on the regular inflight menu were: - Stir-fried seafood with black pepper sauce and Chinese greens over rice - Braised lamb in brown sauce with crushed peas and mint, roasted carrots and Kipfler potatoes The other preorder "Book the Cook" dishes included: - Seafood casarecce in cream sauce - Malay-style nasi lemak coconut rice with spicy sambal prawns, anchovy, roasted peanuts and hard-boiled egg - Braised lamb in red wine sauce with buttery mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables - A selection of special meals for specific dietary requirements Because I'd ordered ahead, my meal was served first — about 20 minutes before other passengers, and just 30 minutes into the flight — so I was finished by the time meal service began for everyone else. That meant sitting around with an empty tray for quite a while, but it was picked up when everyone else's was. About 90 minutes before landing, the second meal service was more of a "refreshment" according to the menu. It included a choice of: - Chicken and mixed vegetable pastie pie - Pea, pumpkin and chickpea samosas with chutney on the side I chose the samosa, and it was hot, delicious and not overly filling. Overall, both meal services were efficient, and the choices were interesting. Not only that, but flight attendants passed through at regular intervals offering passengers beverages (pretty much anything on the menu, not just coffee, water, or tea), which made the experience feel more like business class than economy. Would you recommend Singapore Airlines premium economy? Singapore Airlines premium economy remains an enjoyable experience with spacious seats, solid entertainment options and, thanks to the small cabin size, personalized and polished service from the flight attendants. Among the elements I most appreciated were the seats' significant recline, the option to use a pared-down version of the airline's signature "Book the Cook" meal preorder service and the free Wi-Fi. I do wish the airline would release more saver-level awards on routes, but given the small upsell compared to economy awards, redeeming a few thousand extra miles for tickets that would otherwise be significantly more expensive feels like a worthwhile splurge. item.title: Q3 Amex Platinum credits expire soon — here's how to use them
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.50
Q3 Amex Platinum credits expire soon — here's how to use them Editor's Note If you already have one of American Express' top-tier cards — or are considering applying — the real value comes from how consistently you use its built-in statement credits. As the end of the quarter approaches, it's worth making sure you've used your Q3 statement credits before Sept. 30, alongside any monthly statement credits that reset soon. This guide shows how to make the most of these benefits. Why this matters With a mix of monthly, quarterly and biannual statement credits, both the $895 annual fee American Express Platinum Card® and $895 annual fee The Business Platinum Card® from American Express can deliver hundreds of dollars in value each year (see rates and fees for the Amex Platinum; see rates and fees for the Amex Business Platinum). But that's only if you stay organized and use them before they expire. The consumer Platinum Card offers up to $75 in statement credits for purchases at U.S. Lululemon retail stores (excluding outlets) and online each quarter and up to $100 in statement credits for U.S. Resy-affiliated restaurants each quarter (enrollment required for both benefits). Similarly, the business version of the Platinum Card comes with a suite of ongoing statement credits that can deliver consistent value throughout the year. Advice for Platinum Card members With the up to $75 quarterly Lululemon statement credits and up to $100 quarterly U.S. Resy statement credits, Platinum Card members can extract up to $175 in value from their card's quarterly statement credits. It's essential that both new and existing cardmembers activate their Lululemon and Resy benefits in their Amex account before making any purchases to ensure these perks trigger correctly. Once you activate these benefits, use your card to spend: - Up to $75 at U.S. Lululemon retail stores (excluding outlets) and online: My advice is to click through a shopping portal and browse deals in the secondhand and "We Made Too Much" sale sections. Both online and in-store purchases are eligible for this statement credit (excluding outlets). - Up to $100 at a U.S. Resy restaurant: Look for a participating restaurant in your area; you don't need a reservation to be eligible to receive this statement credit. If you want to combine this quarter's statement credit with a future quarter's statement credit, a useful workaround is to identify a participating restaurant where you can purchase a gift card online. In practice, this allows you to "carry forward" value. You could purchase a gift card during this quarter to trigger the statement credit, then add more to the same gift card next quarter to use up the next statement credit. When you eventually dine at the restaurant, you can redeem the combined balance. This approach can be especially helpful if you don't plan to dine at a participating restaurant before your current quarter's statement credit expires but want to maximize the overall value across multiple quarters. Advice for Business Platinum Card members This is also a good reminder for both new and existing Business Platinum Card members to get up to $140 in value from the following statement credits before the end of the quarter (enrollment required): - Up to a $90 quarterly Indeed statement credit: Use this statement credit for U.S. purchases with Indeed. - Up to a $50 quarterly statement credit on eligible purchases with Hilton: First, make sure to enroll in the Hilton for Business program (for free). Then, use your card to pay for room rates and incidental charges at a Hilton property. Data points suggest you may also be able to receive the Hilton statement credit when dining at a restaurant or purchasing a product from a gift store located within a Hilton property, even if you're not staying at the hotel. I used my Q3 credit to cover $50 of the $59 cost of a high tea for a friend and me at the Urso Hotel & Spa in Madrid — even though we weren't staying at the property. Again, make sure you enroll in these perks first so your purchases trigger these benefits. A note on the semiannual hotel statement credit Both the Platinum Card and the Business Platinum provide an up to $300 semiannual hotel statement credit (up to $600 per calendar year). You'll receive the statement credit on prepaid American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts or The Hotel Collection bookings made through American Express Travel® when you pay with your eligible Platinum Card. (The Hotel Collection stays require a two-night minimum.) Dec. 30 is the deadline to use the second semiannual hotel statement credit (up to $300). If you haven't already used your up to $300 statement credit for the July-to-December period, now is a good time to do so. If you don't have immediate travel planned, you can use the current semiannual statement credit to book a prepaid stay into 2027. I've used my second statement credit for the year to book a stay in Melbourne, Australia, during the holidays. New cardmember? Get an instant card number If you want to pick up the Amex Platinum, you can apply online and get an instant card number for online purchases. You can add it to your digital wallet to use while you wait up to seven business days for your physical card to arrive in the mail. When you apply, you can find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 175,000 bonus points after spending $12,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. (Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.) Then, you can immediately enroll in the statement credits that you can maximize before the end of the quarter. New Amex Business Platinum Card members can find out their offer and see if they are eligible for as high as 300,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. (Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.) Like consumer Amex Platinum Card members, Business Platinum Card members can receive an instant card number upon approval and start maximizing their quarterly statement credits immediately. An important note on contactless payments The terms and conditions for most Amex statement credits say something like this: "The transaction may not be eligible if the merchant uses a third-party to process or submit the transaction to American Express (e.g. using mobile or wireless card readers)." In practice, this means it's not guaranteed that every eligible purchase will trigger a statement credit, depending on how the transaction is processed. I ran into this issue twice when using the semiannual up to $50 Resy statement credits at U.S. Resy restaurants on my (now canceled) American Express® Gold Card — neither transaction posted within the standard eight- to 10-week time frame (enrollment required). After waiting 10 weeks, I contacted Amex via chat and had the statement credits manually applied. Because of this, it's worth keeping an eye on your account. If a statement credit doesn't appear within 10 weeks, reach out to Amex to have it reviewed. And before dining, you may also want to check that the restaurant can process your payment directly (for example, via the card terminal) or ask staff to manually input your card details. Bottom line By being strategic about timing, those with the Amex Platinum or the Business Platinum can take advantage of their statement credits before the end of the quarter. Remember to enroll in benefits before making purchases, track your statement credits throughout the year and follow up if any don't post within several weeks. Finally, I encourage new cardmembers to apply now, jot down their instant card number and immediately add it to their digital wallet. To learn more, read our full reviews of the American Express Platinum and the American Express Business Platinum. Apply now: American Express Platinum Card Apply now: The Business Platinum Card from American Express For rates and fees of the American Express Platinum, click here. For rates and fees of the American Express Business Platinum, click here.
